Author: M.Laxman
Bench: M.Laxman
 The Honourable Sri Justice M.Laxman
 Criminal Petition No.5090 Of 2023
Order:
1.
This petition is filed seeking anticipatory bail under Section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (Cr.P.C).

The petitioner herein is accused No.7 in Crime No. 65 of 2023 of Station House Officer,
Yacharam Police Station, Rachakonda.

The offences alleged against the petitioner/ accused No.7 are under Sections 420 and 406 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code, Section 5 of Telangana State Protection of Depositors of Financial Establishment Act, 1999 and Sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 of Prize and Chit Money Circulation Schemes banning Act, 1978.

sentences.text:
2. The sum and substance of case of the prosecution is that Accused Nos.1 to 5 floated Axis E Corp.
Solutions Private Limited and Accused Nos.6 and 7 attracted to the schemes and they were involved in the promotion of business of Accused Nos.1 to 5 and believed the customers to join in the scheme run by Accused Nos.1 to 5, which is headquartered at Noida.

entities.text:
Axis E Corp.
Solutions Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The allegation is that Rs.15 crores amounts were collected from various customers through their scheme.

Rs.9 Crores were deposited in the accounts of Accused Nos.1 to 5 and with the balance amount of Rs.6 Crores, Accused No.6 and petitioner/ Accused No.7 who are brothers, allegedly purchased various properties.
When the promises were not complied in terms of the scheme, the present complaint has been filed.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner/accused No.7 submitted that petitioner/Accused No.7 the petitioner himself is a victim and he is innocent of the allegations.
Victims were joined voluntarily on their own choice and it is also contended that the provisions of Telangana State Protection of Depositors of Financial Establishment Act is not made out.

entities.text: Telangana State Protection of Depositors of Financial Establishment Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor opposed the bail by contending that the amount of Rs.15 crores were collected through Accused Nos.6 and 7 and Rs.9 Crores were transferred to the account of Accused Nos.1 to 5 and the balance amount was used by the petitioner/Accused No.7 and his brother Accused No.6 to purchase various properties.
5. The investigation reveals prima facie
that amount of Rs.15 crores were collected at the behest of Accused Nos.6 and 7 who are brothers and various amounts were collected from various customers with a promise to provide good returns.
In fact, there is no such authority to Accused Nos.1 to 5 to collect money in terms of guidelines of Reserve Bank of India.
The allegation is that out of Rs.15 crores, Rs.6 were used by the petitioner/accused No.7 and his brother/Accused No.6 and they purchased various properties with the said money.

In view of such serious allegations, this Court feels that the custodial interrogation of the petitioner/Accused No.7 is required and it is not a fit case to grant the relief of anticipatory bail to the petitioner/accused No.7.
7.
Accordingly, the Criminal petition is dismissed.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
